title: 8.2: Run-Time Power Management System by on-Die Power Sensor with Silicon Machine Learning-Based Calibration in a 3nm Octa-Core CPU
problem: High-performance CPUs for gaming face over-current excursions when peak current exceeds PMIC tolerance due to shorter power-budgeting intervals (<50µs at 90fps) and rising CPU clock speeds, causing system instability and performance degradation.
method: The 3nm octa-core CPU integrates on-die power sensors with machine learning-based calibration to enable real-time power management at sub-50µs intervals, dynamically allocating tasks to cores based on instantaneous power budgets to prevent peak-current violations.

title: ZenLeak: Practical Last-Level Cache Side-Channel Attacks on AMD Zen Processors
problem: AMD's non-inclusive caches have been assumed resistant to LLC side-channel attacks due to reverse-engineering challenges; practical attack feasibility on Zen processors remains undemonstrated.
method: ZenLeak reverse-engineers AMD's cache addressing for L2 set index, L3 slice, and L3 set index; constructs eviction sets for non-inclusive caches by solving eviction patterns; demonstrates first LLC side-channel attack on AMD Zen CPUs via OpenSSL AES T-table.

title: In-Memory Arithmetic: Enabling Division with Stochastic Logic
problem: Efficient hardware division has been a long-standing challenge; traditional binary approaches require multiple cycles and complex control logic. Emerging in-memory computing faces additional obstacles: noise sensitivity, process variation, and the inherent difficulty of binary operations in noisy substrates.
method: The approach uses stochastic computing (SC) to implement division within an MTJ-based in-memory architecture; SC represents numbers as bitstreams and performs arithmetic through simple logic operations, naturally tolerating noise. MTJ memory provides the substrate for logic-in-memory operations, reducing the data movement penalty.

title: Hybe: GPU-NPU Hybrid System for Efficient LLM Inference with Million-Token Context Window
problem: LLM inference with million-token context windows is infeasible on GPUs alone because KV cache activation memory for long contexts (>100K tokens) exceeds total GPU DRAM capacity, making batching impractical and leaving GPU compute cores severely underutilized during the memory-bandwidth-bound decode stage. The compute-memory imbalance between compute-intensive prefill and memory-intensive decode cannot be addressed by batching when KV data dominates physical memory.
method: Hybe assigns the compute-intensive prefill stage to existing high-throughput GPUs (NVIDIA H100 with vLLM) and offloads the memory-bandwidth-bound decode stage to lightweight NPUs sized with exactly enough compute to saturate their HBM bandwidth. The key mechanism is fine-grained KV transmission: as the GPU produces partial KV activations during prefill, it immediately streams them to NPU HBM over interconnect, reducing peak GPU memory footprint dramatically. A stage-wise pipeline scheduler dynamically assigns incoming requests to idle GPU or NPU hardware, minimizing pipeline stalls across the two-stage heterogeneous system. Hybe NPU is implemented in 4nm process with HBM matching the H100 HBM specification.

title: AccelES: Accelerating Top-K SpMV for Embedding Similarity via Low-bit Pruning
problem: Top-K sparse matrix-vector multiplication (SpMV) for recommendation system embedding similarity suffers from high latency due to inefficient memory access patterns when scanning full-precision sparse matrices to identify the most relevant embeddings.
method: AccelES employs a two-stage computation scheme: Stage 1 uses a compact low-bit (pruned) representation of the sparse matrix to rapidly identify the top-K candidate entries with minimal data movement, and Stage 2 performs full-precision SpMV only on this pruned candidate subset. Two novel sparse matrix storage formats, Ultra-CSR and Random-CSR, are introduced to optimize memory bandwidth utilization for irregular access patterns inherent in SpMV. The low-bit approximation in Stage 1 filters out irrelevant entries early, reducing the volume of full-precision computation dramatically.

title: FireGuard: A Generalized Microarchitecture for Fine-Grained Security Analysis on OoO Superscalar Cores
problem: Generic programmable support for fine-grained instruction-level security analysis on real out-of-order (OoO) superscalar processors; existing abstract simulators cannot capture critical path and contention issues in real microarchitectures.
method: FireGuard microarchitecture for fine-grained instruction analysis on real OoO superscalar cores, including: microarchitecture design, SoC integration, ISA extensions, and programming model. Addresses challenges of programmable pathways without adding critical path or contention. Feasibility analyzed on Apple M1-Pro, Huawei Kirin-960, and Intel i7-12700F.

title: 15.1 A 3.9mW 200words/min Neural Signal Processor in Speech Decoding for Brain-Machine Interface
problem: Speech-based brain-machine interfaces require real-time neural network inference on implanted devices with ultra-low power budgets; existing high-end CPUs consume 65 W and require 5.3 seconds to decode a single word, making implantable BMI impractical.
method: A dedicated neural signal processor that maps the speech-decoding neural network (phone probability inference followed by beam-search word decoding using a language model) onto a specialized hardware pipeline. The design combines efficient NN inference blocks with language-model lookup acceleration to decode at 200 words/min.

title: LLMShare: Optimizing LLM Inference Serving with Hardware Architecture Exploration
problem: LLM serving systems use fixed hardware configurations that don't differentiate between the prefill phase (high parallelism, compute-bound) and decoding phase (low parallelism, memory-bandwidth-bound), leading to resource waste and high serving costs.
method: Develops a simulator modeling performance and cost across heterogeneous hardware configurations (CPUs, GPUs, accelerators), then applies design space exploration to find the Pareto-optimal allocation of resources to prefill vs. decoding stages. Aligns hardware capabilities with specific phase demands.

title: Assessing Quantum Layout Synthesis Tools via Known Optimal-SWAP Cost Benchmarks
problem: Quantum layout synthesis (QLS) tools insert SWAP gates to satisfy hardware connectivity constraints; existing SWAP-free benchmarks have known-optimal depths but do not evaluate SWAP count performance. Real-world applications require SWAP gates, leaving QLS tool quality assessment incomplete.
method: Introduces QUBIKOS, a benchmark set with provably-optimal SWAP counts and non-trivial circuit structures. Evaluates leading QLS tools (LightSabre, ML-QLS, QMAP, tket) against known-optimal baselines, revealing large optimality gaps. Analysis of suboptimal cases provides insights for future algorithm design.

title: 15.3 A 65nm Uncertainty-Quantifiable Ventricular Arrhythmia Detection Engine with 1.75µJ Per Inference
problem: Deep-learning based ventricular arrhythmia detection for implantable cardioverter defibrillators (ICDs) lacks transparency in uncertainty quantification (UQ), limiting clinical reliability; Bayesian neural networks address this but incur >6x energy overhead from Gaussian random number generation and multiple sampling iterations.
method: The 65nm Bayes-CNN accelerator implements fully parallel analog Gaussian random number generation (GRNG), in-memory vector-matrix operations using analog circuits, and partial sampling strategies to reduce energy overhead of uncertainty quantification in convolutional neural networks for VA classification.

title: Move Less, Retrieve Fast: A Retrieval-in-Memory Architecture for Language Models
problem: Retrieval-augmented language models (RALMs) suffer from substantial data movement and irregular access patterns during retrieval, limiting efficiency on conventional CPU/GPU architectures.
method: Rimast architecture combines 3D-stacked processing-in-memory (PIM) hardware with hardware-software co-design. Hierarchical PIM dataflow minimizes data transfer between memory and compute. Software layers include skew-free data mapping for uniform distribution and adaptive offloading strategies to handle irregular access patterns in RALM retrieval.

title: 8.1 Dynamic Guard-Band Features of the IBM zNext System
problem: Fixed voltage guard bands at each supported frequency must cover all variation sources (power-supply droops, temperature excursions, device aging), consuming significant power even when worst-case conditions do not occur.
method: Full system that simultaneously leverages robust droop mitigation (e.g., on-chip power delivery management) and robust error recovery (e.g., voltage-independent correction codes or timeout mechanisms) to reduce required voltage margins in real-time using on-chip sensors and firmware.

title: 21.6 A 2A Fully Analog Distribution LDO with Noise Immunity for an SoC
problem: Analog distribution LDOs (DISLDOs) for SoCs suffer from noise coupling on analog control signals between distributed power transistors, resulting in excessive output voltage ripple and preventing practical deployment in advanced SoCs.
method: A fully analog DISLDO design incorporates noise-immune analog signal distribution and transmission techniques to maintain even current distribution across power transistors despite high on-chip noise, achieving 2A output current with stable regulation.

title: The Importance of Generalizability in Machine Learning for Systems
problem: ML models deployed in cloud system management tasks frequently encounter out-of-distribution (OOD) data — workloads or resource demand patterns not represented in training data — causing silent mispredictions that degrade server resource balance without any indication of model unreliability.
method: The paper analyzes several ML models used for resource balance in Google's production fleet, empirically demonstrating OOD failure modes. It evaluates multiple OOD detection techniques (distance-based, confidence-based, ensemble methods) and quantifies their trade-offs in precision, recall, and inference overhead. It then demonstrates that Bayesian models — which produce calibrated uncertainty estimates over their outputs — can effectively flag low-confidence predictions to a human operator or fallback policy, improving reliability of ML-driven resource balancing.

title: throttLL'eM: Predictive GPU Throttling for Energy Efficient LLM Inference Serving
problem: LLM inference serving on GPUs consumes excessive energy while providers must simultaneously satisfy Service-Level Objectives (SLOs); static GPU frequency settings over-provision compute resources when request load is low or KV cache pressure is manageable.
method: throttLL'eM uses instance sizing and GPU frequency scaling guided by an ML model that predicts future KV cache usage and batch size. The ML model receives projections of these metrics as inputs and outputs per-iteration performance estimates, enabling iteration-level frequency decisions. The R^2 score exceeds 0.97 and misprediction is under 1 iteration/second on average. Frequency scaling and instance count adjustments are applied jointly to reduce energy while keeping within SLO bounds.

title: PastATPG: A Hybrid ATPG Framework for Better Test Compaction with Partial Assignment SAT
problem: SAT-based ATPG generates complete assignments for all primary inputs in fanin cone, leading to pattern inflation and excessive runtime; test compaction becomes intractable as circuits grow.
method: PA-MiniSat SAT solver enabling partial assignments instead of complete assignments; full-literal watching technique and circuit-adapted branching heuristics; hybrid ATPG framework tightly integrating structural algorithms with PA-MiniSat.
